authoredSolutions.151: \(f(x)=|2x^2+5|x|-3|\) is continuous everywhere, so \(m=0\). Let \(g(x)=2x^2+5|x|-3\); \(g\) has a corner at \(x=0\) (\(g'(0^\pm)=\pm5\)) but \(g(0)=-3\ne0\), so \(f=|g|\) is non-differentiable at \(x=0\). authoredSolutions.152: For \(px^2+qx-r=0\): \(\alpha+\beta=-q/p,\ \alpha\beta=-r/p\). GP gives \(q^2=pr\). \(\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha\beta}=\frac{q}{r}=\frac34\). With ratio \(k\): \(q=pk,r=pk^2\Rightarrow q/r=1/k=3/4\Rightarrow k=4/3\). Then \(\alpha+\beta=-k=-\tfrac43,\ \alpha\beta=-k^2=-\tfrac{16}{9}\). \((\alpha-\beta)^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-4\alpha\beta=\tfrac{16}{9}+\tfrac{64}{9}=\tfrac{80}{9}\).
authoredSolutions.153: Using \(\sin^2x=1-\cos^2x\): \(4(1-\cos^2x)-4\cos^3x+9-4\cos x=0\Rightarrow 4\cos^3x+4\cos^2x+4\cos x-13=0\). authoredSolutions.178: Curves \(x=\tfrac{2y^2}{k}\) and \(x=y-\tfrac{k y^2}{2}\) meet at \(y=0\) and \(y^*=\tfrac{2k}{k^2+4}\).
